complete_examples.text: However, the characteristic wavelengths have a dramatic impact on the interactions between railway vehicles and tracks, especially when the irregularity amplitudes are at the boundary conditions.
Therefore, the characteristic wavelengths can be calculated using Eq. (58).
Finally, a method is developed to precisely extract the characteristic wavelengths and amplitude limits of track irregularities.
Using the same procedure, other characteristic wavelengths can be clarified.

In the present work, a track irregularity characteristic wavelengths based method is proposed to predict track sections where the wheel-rail forces will be aggravated due to the irregularities of the track profiles.

For example, the energy density at the track position of around 500 m, as shown in Fig. 15(a), is of big magnitude, but actually, the corresponding wheel/ rail force is not that large, the reason of which may lie in the influence of waveforms or crossing combination of characteristic wavelengths on wheel/rail interactions.
